ExportResumeState.description:
Serializable state needed to resume an invoice export after a restart.

``ExportJob.resume_state()`` returns it and ``auth.invoices.export(state=...)``
turns it back into an ``ExportJob``. It holds the AES key and IV that decrypt
the package, so treat ``to_json()`` and ``to_dict()`` output as credential
material. ``model_dump()`` and ``repr()`` redact the secrets and are not a
persistence format.
ExportResumeState.title: ExportResumeState

ExportedInvoicesData.description:
Portable snapshot of a completed invoice export.

``ExportedInvoices.to_model()`` returns it and ``ExportedInvoices.from_model()``
turns it back into a result, so a finished export can be handed to another
process or language binding. ``archive`` holds the joined ZIP or TarGz bytes and
is URL-safe Base64 in JSON, carrying the standard ``=`` padding whenever the
archive length is not a multiple of three; ``package`` and ``metadata`` carry
the package metadata and the parsed ``_metadata.json`` records.

``model_dump()``, ``model_dump_json()`` and ``repr()`` keep ``PackagePart.url``
redacted, so for a package that still has parts they are a view and not a
persistence format: a presigned URL is a capability, and the generic dump drops
it. Use ``to_sensitive_dict()`` and ``to_sensitive_json()`` when the whole
package must travel, and protect that output like a credential. Restoring a
result needs no network access and no keys: the archive is already decrypted.
ExportedInvoicesData.title: ExportedInvoicesData

XAdESCredentials.description:
Certificate and private key for ``with_xades()``, held as normalized data.

Build it with :meth:`from_pem`, :meth:`from_der` or :meth:`from_pkcs12` and pass
the result as ``with_xades(nip=..., credentials=...)``. The constructors accept
raw bytes rather than file paths, so a caller that reads the files, receives an
upload or crosses a language boundary keeps control of the transport.

Whatever the input format, the model stores the certificate as PEM and the key
as unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM. The key field is a ``SecretBytes`` excluded from
``model_dump()``, ``model_dump_json()`` and ``repr()``, so a generic dump is a
display form and never a credential export: it cannot be read back. The password
is consumed while decoding and is not stored anywhere on the model, so there is
no retained password to leak and none to rotate.

Note:
    Because the stored key is unencrypted PEM in memory, the model is a secret.
    Keep it out of logs, caches and persistence, and drop the reference when
    authentication is done. Use it for nothing but the call that signs.

Example:
    ```python
    from pathlib import Path

    from ksef2.xades import XAdESCredentials

    credentials = XAdESCredentials.from_pem(
        Path("company.pem").read_bytes(),
        Path("company.key").read_bytes(),
    )
    auth = client.authentication.with_xades(
        nip="5261040828", credentials=credentials
    )
    ```
XAdESCredentials.title: XAdESCredentials
